# File formats {#sec-formats}

`BIYOS_readmdl` and `Model.read` read a model from a file in the format the caller names, and `BIYOS_writemdl` and `Model.write` write one. This chapter gives the rules of each format as the reader applies them, then the rules of the writer. A file that breaks one gives `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE`, a section or segment the reader does not handle gives `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, each oddity the reader reads past is a warning event from module `io`, with the fields `file` and `line`, and each part it skips is an info event with the same fields. In the binary part of an NL file, `byte` takes the place of `line`.

## Free MPS

`BIYOS_FILEFMT_MPS` reads free MPS, the form of MPS in which fields are separated by white space and names hold no blanks. The rules below are those of the CPLEX [MPS reference](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/icos/22.1.2?topic=standard-records-in-mps-format) and the Gurobi [MPS reference](https://docs.gurobi.com/projects/optimizer/en/current/reference/fileformats/modelformats.html#mps-format), where the two agree. Where they differ or say nothing, biyos sets its own rule, given in [Choices](#sec-mps-choices).

### Lines

A line that starts with `*` is a comment. A section line starts in the first column with the name of its section. A data line starts with a blank, and its fields are separated by white space. In a data line, a third or fifth field that starts with `$` makes the rest of the line a comment. Numbers are written in decimal or exponential notation.

### Sections

The sections come in this order: `NAME`, `OBJSENSE`, `ROWS`, `COLUMNS`, `RHS`, `RANGES`, `BOUNDS`, `SOS`, `INDICATORS`, `ENDATA`. `OBJSENSE`, `RANGES`, `BOUNDS`, `SOS` and `INDICATORS` may be left out. A file without `RHS` gives a warning and sets every right-hand side to 0. `ENDATA` is the last line.

| Section | Holds |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | The name of the model, on the same line. |
| `OBJSENSE` | `MAX` to maximize, on the same line or the next. Minimization when left out. `OBJSEN` is the same section. |
| `ROWS` | A sense letter and a name for each row. |
| `COLUMNS` | A column name, then one or two pairs of a row name and a coefficient. |
| `RHS` | A vector name, then one or two pairs of a row name and a value. |
| `RANGES` | A vector name, then one or two pairs of a row name and a range. |
| `BOUNDS` | A bound type, a vector name, a column name and a value. |
| `SOS` | A set line with a type and a name, then a line for each member with a column name and a weight. |
| `INDICATORS` | `IF`, a row name, a column name and the value 0 or 1. |

### Rows

Each row has a sense: `N` free, `L` less than or equal, `G` greater than or equal, `E` equality. The first `N` row is the objective. A row the `RHS` section leaves out has a right-hand side of 0. A right-hand side on the objective row is the negative of the objective's offset.

A range turns a row into an interval. With right-hand side $r$ and range $R$:

| Sense | Lower | Upper |
|---|---|---|
| `G` | $r$ | $r + \lvert R \rvert$ |
| `L` | $r - \lvert R \rvert$ | $r$ |
| `E`, $R \ge 0$ | $r$ | $r + R$ |
| `E`, $R < 0$ | $r + R$ | $r$ |

Only the first vector of `RHS`, of `RANGES` and of `BOUNDS` is read.

### Columns

The lines of one column are contiguous. Columns between a marker line `'MARKER'` `'INTORG'` and a marker line `'MARKER'` `'INTEND'` are integer, with bounds 0 and 1 when the `BOUNDS` section gives them none. A file may hold any number of marker pairs.

### Bounds

A column has a lower bound of 0 and no upper bound unless the `BOUNDS` section says otherwise.

| Type | Effect |
|---|---|
| `LO` | Lower bound. |
| `UP` | Upper bound. |
| `FX` | Lower and upper bound, both the value. |
| `FR` | Free: no lower and no upper bound. |
| `MI` | No lower bound. |
| `PL` | No upper bound. |
| `BV` | Binary. The value is 1 or left out. |
| `LI` | Integer, with the value as lower bound. The value is an integer. |
| `UI` | Integer, with the value as upper bound. The value is an integer. |
| `SC` | Semi-continuous, with the value as upper bound. The value is given. |
| `SI` | Semi-integer, with the value as upper bound. |

Both documents list the types. The rules on the values of `BV`, `LI`, `UI` and `SC` are those of CPLEX's table of integer bound types; `SI` is Gurobi's.

An upper bound below 0 on a column with no other bound sets its lower bound to minus infinity, with a warning.

### Sets

A set line starts with `S1` for a special ordered set of type 1 or `S2` for type 2, followed by the name of the set. Each line after it names a column of the set and its weight. A column appears in a set once, and no two members of a set share a weight.

### Indicators

An indicator line names a row of sense `L`, `G` or `E` and a binary column. The row holds while the column takes the value the line gives. The row becomes a function and an indicator on it with the row's bounds, and no constraint; its name is not kept. Several indicator lines may name one row, each giving an indicator on its function.

### Choices {#sec-mps-choices}

Each rule below is biyos's rule. The document it follows is named where there is one.

| Case | biyos's rule |
|---|---|
| No `N` row | The model has no objective. Neither document requires an `N` row. |
| `N` rows after the first | Each is a constraint on its function with no lower and no upper bound. CPLEX discards them. |
| `OBJNAME`, or an `N` row with objective fields | Refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`. |
| A second right-hand side or range on a row | Refused, within the vector read. |
| A range on an `N` row | Ignored, with a warning. The CPLEX range table covers `G`, `L` and `E` rows only. |
| A column that crosses a marker line | Refused: a column lies wholly inside or wholly outside an integer block. |
| Several vectors in `RHS`, `RANGES` or `BOUNDS` | Only the first is read, as CPLEX states; the first line of each later vector gives a warning. Gurobi ignores the vector names. |
| Bounds of a marked column | 0 and 1 when the `BOUNDS` section gives none, as CPLEX states. Once one bound is given, the other takes its default for any column: 0 for the lower, no upper bound. Gurobi keeps the upper bound at 1. |
| Two lower or two upper bounds on a column | Refused. `FX` gives both, so `FX` and `UP` on one column are two upper bounds. |
| `SI` without a value | Refused, as CPLEX refuses `SC` without one. |
| Negative upper bound | CPLEX's rule above holds for every type that sets the upper bound alone: `UP`, `UI`, `SC` and `SI`. |
| A value on `FR`, `MI` or `PL` | It is ignored, with a warning. |
| `OBJSENSE` | `MAX` and `MIN`, on the same line as Gurobi writes it or on the next as CPLEX does. Neither document states `MIN`. |
| Numbers | Decimal or exponential, the sign of the exponent optional. A missing exponent, which CPLEX reads as 0, is refused, as is a value outside the range of a double. The 25-character limit of CPLEX is not checked. |
| Infinity | Neither document gives an MPS spelling of infinity, so a word such as `inf` is refused. `1e30` and larger finite values are read as written; an infinite bound is set with `MI`, `PL` or `FR`. |
| A set line | A set line and a member line differ in free MPS by their first field alone, so a line whose first field is `S1` or `S2` starts a set. |
| A set without a name | It is read without one, as CPLEX allows. Gurobi gives every set a name. |
| A member without a weight | Its weight is its position in the set, counted from 1, as CPLEX states for a set with no reference row. |
| A repeated member or weight in a set | Refused. CPLEX states that the weights of a set are distinct. |
| `SOSORG` markers and `REFROW` | Not read. CPLEX's other form of sets is refused as unsupported: a marker line ending `'SOSORG'` or `'SOSEND'`, and the section `REFROW`. |
| Order of `SOS` and `INDICATORS` | `SOS` comes first, as in Gurobi's description. CPLEX gives no order between the two. |
| An indicator on an integer column | A column of kind integer with bounds 0 and 1, such as one between marker lines with no bound, becomes binary, as CPLEX counts marker lines as a way to declare one. Any other column that is not binary is refused. |
| An indicator on an `N` row or a row with a range | Refused. CPLEX allows `L`, `G` and `E` rows and no row with a range. |

### Writing {#sec-mps-writing}

`BIYOS_FILEFMT_MPS` writes free MPS that the reader above reads back to the same model, every number bit for bit but a constant of $-0$, which reads back as 0. The file is made or replaced.

| Part | Written as |
|---|---|
| Sections | `NAME`, then `OBJSENSE MAX` on one line when the objective maximizes, `ROWS`, `COLUMNS`, `RHS`, `ENDATA`. `RANGES` only when a row has a range, `BOUNDS` only when a column needs a bound line, `SOS` only when the model has a set, `INDICATORS` only when it has an indicator. |
| Name | The model's name after `NAME`, or `NAME` alone when it has none. |
| Numbers | The shortest decimal or exponential form that reads back to the same double. An infinite bound is a bound type, never a number. |
| Objective | The first `N` row, with the negative of its constant as right-hand side. It comes before the first constraint whose function is its own or a later one, so the objective of a model read from MPS reads back on the same function. When a free constraint would come before it, it comes first, since the reader takes the first `N` row as the objective. |
| No objective | No objective row. When a constraint is free, an empty `N` row comes first, so the model reads back with an objective of 0. |
| Constraints | One row each, in order. A constant moves into the bounds, $l - c$ and $u - c$, so the row reads back with no constant. The sense is `E`, `L` or `G` from the bounds, `G` or `L` with a range for an interval, `N` for a free constraint. |
| Columns | One column per variable, in order. A variable in no row is a column line holding its name alone. Variables of kind integer lie between marker lines. |
| Bounds | `BV` for a binary variable, `SC` or `SI` for the upper bound of a semi-continuous or semi-integer one, `FX` for equal bounds, else `LO` or `MI` and `UP` or `PL`. |
| Names | Each record keeps its name. An unnamed objective is `OBJ`, an unnamed constraint `R` and an unnamed variable `C`, each followed by its index. While a user name holds the label, `_1`, `_2` and so on is added. |
| Sets | A set line with the type and the name, or the type alone for an unnamed set, then one line for each member with its weight, in order. |
| Indicators | One row for each function and bounds, after the constraints, its sense from the bounds as for a constraint, named `I` and the index of its first indicator with the suffix rule of names, then a line in `INDICATORS` for each indicator. Indicators on one function with the same bounds share its row, as several lines naming one row read back. The name of an indicator is left out. |
| Functions | A function several records use is written once for each, and reads back as that many functions. A function no record uses is left out. |

The writer refuses with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, naming the first record in the way:

- a second objective, or a weight other than 1 on the only one;
- quadratic terms, an expression, a callback, a cone or a complement;
- an indicator whose bounds are two distinct finite values or both infinite, which no indicator row holds, or one on a function a constraint uses;
- a name two variables share, or two rows among the objective and the constraints;
- a name that holds white space or starts with `$`, a row named `'MARKER'`, a set member named `S1` or `S2`, a model name that starts or ends with white space or holds a line break;
- a binary variable with bounds other than 0 and 1, a semi-continuous or semi-integer variable with no upper bound;
- constraint bounds no row reads back exactly, or that overflow once the constant moves into them.

A path that cannot be opened or written gives `BIYOS_ERR_FILEIO`. Each part the format cannot hold is left out with one warning event from module `io`, with the field `file`, sent once the file is written: the tolerances of variables and constraints, the tolerances and the priority of the objective, the names of indicators, and the model's options. Hooks are not part of the problem and are left out with no event.

## Fixed MPS {#sec-mps-fixed}

`BIYOS_FILEFMT_FIXMPS` reads fixed MPS, the form of MPS in which each field of a data line starts in a set column and names may hold blanks. Every rule of free MPS above holds but the split of a data line into fields. The columns are those of the Gurobi [MPS reference](https://docs.gurobi.com/projects/optimizer/en/current/reference/fileformats/modelformats.html#mps-format), which states where each field starts; the CPLEX reference describes fields separated by white space alone. Fixed MPS is read, never written.

| Field | Columns |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 to 4 |
| 2 | 5 to 14 |
| 3 | 15 to 24 |
| 4 | 25 to 39 |
| 5 | 40 to 49 |
| 6 | 50 to the end of the line |

A section line is read as in free MPS, with the model name the rest of the `NAME` line. In a data line, the blanks at either end of a field are dropped and those inside it are part of the name. A data line whose field 1 is blank holds the fields from field 2 on, as a free MPS line in `COLUMNS`, `RHS` or `RANGES` does. Empty fields at the end of a line are left out, and one before a field that is not empty stays empty: a vector name of `RHS`, `RANGES` or `BOUNDS` may be blank, while an empty row, column or set member name and an empty value are refused. An `OBJSENSE` data line is one word and is split at white space, as in free MPS.

| Case | biyos's rule |
|---|---|
| Field ends | Gurobi states where each field starts. A field runs to the column before the next one starts, so text too long for its columns runs into the next field. |
| A blank vector name | The empty name, read as any vector name, so a later vector gives the warning of free MPS. Neither document says a vector name may be blank. |
| Blanks in names | Kept inside a name, as Gurobi states for fixed format, and dropped at its ends. |
| Marker lines | A `COLUMNS` line whose second word is `'MARKER'` is split at white space, as in free MPS, since the reader keeps nothing of the marker's name. A marker name with blanks is refused. Gurobi places `'MARKER'` in column 15 and `'INTORG'` or `'INTEND'` in column 40. |
| Tabs | A tab is one column. |
| Long lines | Field 6 runs to the end of the line, so text after it, such as a card number in columns 73 to 80, makes its value unreadable. |

## NL

`BIYOS_FILEFMT_NL` reads NL, the format AMPL writes for a solver, in its text and its binary form. The rules below are those of Gay's description of the format [@gay2005], and for what it leaves out of the binary form, those of the NL reader of AMPL's MP library [@amplmp2026]. Where it says nothing, biyos sets its own rule, given in [Choices](#sec-nl-choices). The writer writes the text form, by the rules in [Writing](#sec-nl-writing).

### Lines

The first field of a line is a letter, often followed by a number in the same field, such as `C3` or `o2`. Fields are separated by white space, and a `#` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. Numbers are written in decimal or exponential notation.

### Header

The file starts with ten lines. The first starts with `g` for text or `b` for binary. The other forms AMPL writes, `h` and `z` for large files and `B`, `G`, `H` and `Z` for debugging, are refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`. The next nine hold counts in the order Gay gives, the second line starting with the numbers of variables, constraints and objectives. The counts fix the kind of each variable from its place in the order of variables in Gay's tables [@gay2017], and every variable they do not mark integer or binary is continuous.

### Binary

The header of a binary file is the same ten lines of text. The third count of its sixth line, `arith`, gives the byte order of what follows: `1` little-endian, `2` big-endian. Any other value is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, `0` among them.

After the header, the file holds the same items as text with no white space and no newlines. A letter, such as a segment key, the key of an expression item or a bound code, is one byte, a bound code being the ASCII digit. An integer is four bytes in two's complement, a number eight bytes in IEEE double precision, and a name a four byte length followed by its bytes. A constant may be `s`, followed by a two byte integer, or `l`, followed by a four byte integer, as well as `n`. A file that ends inside an item gives `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE`, and a message names the byte where the item starts, counted from 0 at the start of the file.

### Segments

After the header, each segment starts with a letter. They may come in any order, but a segment for one record, or a `b`, `r`, `k`, `x` or `d` segment, appears once. Every constraint needs its `C` segment and every objective its `O` segment, and a file with constraints needs `r`, one with variables `b`.

| Segment | Holds |
|---|---|
| `V` | A defined variable: its index, a count of linear terms, the terms, then its expression. |
| `C` | The expression of a constraint. |
| `O` | The expression of an objective and its sense, `0` to minimize and `1` to maximize. |
| `r` | The bounds of each constraint. |
| `b` | The bounds of each variable. |
| `k` | The column lengths of the Jacobian, which are checked for their count alone. |
| `J` | The linear terms of a constraint. |
| `G` | The linear terms of an objective. |
| `x` | A starting point, skipped with an info event. |
| `d` | Dual guesses, skipped with an info event. |
| `S` | A suffix, skipped with an info event naming it, but for the integer suffix `sosno` and the suffix `ref` on variables, which give special ordered sets [@gay2017]. Each nonzero value of `sosno` is a set, of type 1 when it is positive and 2 when negative, and `ref` gives the weight of each member. A real `sosno` is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`. |

A bound line starts with a code: `0` gives a lower and an upper bound, `1` an upper bound, `2` a lower bound, `3` neither and `4` one value for both. In `r`, code `5` with two integers $k$ and $i$ pairs the constraint with variable $i$, from 1, as a complement: its function becomes the second function of the complement, the first is the variable alone, and the bounds are those of the variable, which keeps them. $k$ is 1 when the lower bound is finite, 2 when the upper one is, 3 when both are and 0 when neither is. Code `5` in `b` is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE`, and the segments `F` (imported functions) and `L` (logical constraints) with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`.

### Expressions

An expression is written in prefix order, one item a line: `n` and a number for a constant, `v` and an index for a variable or a defined variable, `o` and a code for an operator followed by its operands. An operator that takes any number of operands, `min`, `max` and `sum`, has its count on the next line.

| Operators | Read as |
|---|---|
| `plus`, `minus`, `sum` | A sum. |
| `mult` | A product. |
| `div` | A division. |
| `less` | $\max(x - y, 0)$: a sum, then `max` with 0. A NaN operand gives NaN. |
| `pow` | A power, with a constant exponent when the exponent is a number. |
| `neg`, `abs`, `min`, `max` | The same operator. |
| `sqrt`, `exp`, `log`, `log10` | The same function, `log10` as the natural logarithm times $\log_{10} e$. |
| `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan` | The same function. |
| `atan2` | The same function, its first operand $y$ in $\operatorname{atan2}(y, x)$. |
| `sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`, `asinh`, `acosh`, `atanh` | The same function. |
| `plterm` | A piecewise linear function of one variable. |

Every other operator, among them the comparisons, the logical operators, `if`, `floor`, `ceil` and `round`, is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, as are imported functions (`f`) and strings (`h`).

### Choices {#sec-nl-choices}

| Case | biyos's rule |
|---|---|
| Header counts | A file must hold at least two bytes for each variable, constraint, objective and defined variable the header counts, one byte in binary, so a short file cannot make the reader allocate for a large model. |
| Several objectives | Each is read, with its sense, and its priority is its place in the file. |
| Names | NL holds none; names in separate files are not read. |
| A linear term with coefficient 0 | Kept as a term of the function. |
| A defined variable | Read once and shared by each expression that uses it. A use before its `V` segment is refused. |
| `plterm` | Slopes and breakpoints become the points of a piecewise linear function that is 0 at 0, as in AMPL, with one more point beyond the first and the last breakpoint so that the end slopes hold. Breakpoints that do not increase are refused. |
| Kinds of variables | The variables used nonlinearly in objectives alone number the second count of the fifth header line less the first, the integer ones among them included. |
| A binary variable | Bounds outside 0 and 1 are refused. |
| A complementarity | A code $k$ that does not match the bounds of its variable is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE`, and a variable paired twice with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, as the writer refuses it. The linear and nonlinear complements of the third header line must add up to the rows code `5` pairs, and to no more than the constraints, or the file is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE`. Complements follow the constraints in the order of their rows. |
| Special ordered sets | Sets are in the order of the absolute value of `sosno`, a positive value before its negative, and members in the order of variables. A set with no member in `ref`, each set when `ref` is absent, has the weights 1, 2, 3 in member order, as `BIYOS_addsos` gives with no weights; in any other set a member `ref` does not list has weight 0. Weights repeated in a set are refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, as a model cannot hold them. `ref` without `sosno`, and either suffix on constraints, objectives or the problem, is skipped with an info event. |

### Writing {#sec-nl-writing}

`BIYOS_FILEFMT_NL` writes the text form, with no comments, which the reader above reads back. The file is made or replaced. Numbers are written in the shortest decimal or exponential form that reads back to the same double, and an infinite bound is a bound code, never a number.

A model read from NL reads back the same, every number bit for bit, when the `J` and `G` segments of its file list each variable that the expressions of their record use, it holds no constant of $-0$, which reads back as 0, and its complements follow the constraints of their group of rows. Any other model reads back with the changes the table gives, which `difference` reports, and reads back the same when written a second time. Among those changes, complements come back in the order of their rows, the function of each one's variable renumbered after every other function, and the members of each set in the order the variables are written.

| Part | Written as |
|---|---|
| Header | `g3 1 1 0`, then the counts of Gay's header. The counts of network constraints and variables, imported functions and name lengths are 0, and the line of `arith` and `flags` is `0 0 0 1`, as in Gay's example. |
| Order of variables | Gay's order [@gay2017]: the variables used nonlinearly in constraints and objectives, then in constraints alone, then in objectives alone, the continuous ones before the integer ones in each, then the linear continuous, binary and integer ones, each group in model order. A binary variable used nonlinearly is written as an integer one with its own bounds. |
| Order of constraints | The constraints whose function has quadratic terms or an expression, then the others, each group in model order, and in each group the constraints before the complements. |
| Complements | A row of the second function, with the line `5` of $k$ and the variable in `r`. The third header line then holds the six counts of the AMPL MP library [@amplmp2026]: those of nonlinear constraints and objectives, linear and nonlinear complements, complements with both bounds finite, and complements with a finite lower bound other than 0. |
| Special ordered sets | An `S0` segment `sosno` at the end of the file gives each member the number of its set, from 1 and negative for type 2. An `S4` segment `ref` follows with every weight, 0 included. |
| Objectives | In model order, each with its sense. Every objective up to the last nonlinear one counts as nonlinear in the header. |
| Bounds | `r` and `b` give each constraint and variable a bound code, in the order above: `4` when the bounds are equal, `3` when both are infinite, `1` or `2` when one is, else `0`. |
| Linear terms | A `J` or `G` segment for each record, with each linear term of its function, then a term of coefficient 0 for each variable its expression uses and no linear term holds. `k` counts the `J` entries of each variable. |
| Expressions | A `C` or `O` segment for each record. A function with no constant and no quadratic terms whose expression is not a sum, or is one written as `plus`, `sum` or `minus`, is its expression alone. Any other is a sum of its constant, one product for each quadratic term, its coefficient a factor when it is not 1, then the expression, written out as its terms when it is a sum with no constant. The reader splits such a sum back into the same parts, and keeps the expression alone whole. |
| Operators | A sum of two or more terms with no constant and weights of 1 is `plus` or `sum`, one of two terms with weights 1 and $-1$ `minus`, any other a `plus` or `sum` of its constant, when it is not 0, and its terms, each weight a factor when it is not 1. A product is a chain of `mult`, its coefficient a factor when it is not 1. A constant power is `pow` with a number. A product of $\log_{10} e$ and a logarithm is `log10`. Every other operator the reader reads is written as the code it reads. |
| Piecewise linear functions | `plterm` with the slopes and the inner breakpoints of the points, plus the value at 0 when it is not 0. The reader rebuilds the points from the slopes, so points whose slopes are not exact in floating point read back moved by a rounding. |
| Defined variables | A node used by several parents, the operand of a piecewise linear function, the constant exponent of a power, and a sum that is not `plus`, `sum` or `minus` and whose terms are variables, or variables then one term of weight 1 with no constant, each written once as a `V` segment and named again. Such a sum has its variables as the linear terms of the segment, the form in which the reader reads a defined variable back. Those used by several records come first, the others just before the segment of their record, with the third integer Gay gives. |
| Functions | A function several records use is written once for each, and reads back as that many functions. A function no record uses is left out, with an info event from module `io`, with the field `file`, naming it. |

The writer refuses with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, naming the first record in the way: a callback, a cone or an indicator; a complement whose first function is not one variable with coefficient 1, whose bounds are not those of that variable, whose variable is free, or whose variable another complement holds; an empty special ordered set, or a variable in two sets; a semi-continuous or semi-integer variable; an objective with a weight other than 1; an expression that holds `BIYOS_OP_ENT`, `BIYOS_OP_SPOW`, `BIYOS_OP_ERF`, `BIYOS_OP_ATAN2`, a comparison, `BIYOS_OP_AND`, `BIYOS_OP_OR`, `BIYOS_OP_NOT` or `BIYOS_OP_IF`.

A path that cannot be opened or written gives `BIYOS_ERR_FILEIO`. Each part the format cannot hold is left out with one warning event from module `io`, with the field `file`, sent once the file is written: the tolerances of variables and constraints, the tolerances and the priority of each objective, and the model's options, as for MPS; then the binary variables written as integers, and the names. Hooks are not part of the problem and are left out with no event.

## Native {#sec-native}

`BIYOS_FILEFMT_BYS` is biyos's own format. It holds every part of a model but its callbacks and its options, and the reader reads a written file back to the same model, every number bit for bit.

### Lines

A line is a record of fields separated by white space. Blank lines are skipped, and no line is a comment. The first line is `BIYOS 1`, the version of the format; a later version is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`. The last line is `END`, and only blank lines may follow it. A word that names no section is refused with `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE`, since every section of the format is read.

| Field | Written as |
|---|---|
| Number | Decimal or exponential, the sign optional, or exactly `inf` or `-inf`. The writer gives the shortest form that reads back to the same double. |
| Index, count | A whole decimal number. Records and variables are counted from 0. |
| Kind, sense, operator | The name of its `BIYOS_` constant after the group, in lowercase: `bin` for `BIYOS_VARKND_BIN`, `min` for `BIYOS_OBJSENSE_MIN`, `soc` for `BIYOS_CONEKND_SOC`, `sin` for `BIYOS_OP_SIN`. A number or a word of another group is refused, and so is `node`: a file is read into a new model, which holds no node to name. |
| Name | One field. A blank, a control byte, the byte 7F and `\` are `\` and two uppercase hexadecimal digits, so `a b` is `a\20b`. Any other byte, those of UTF-8 among them, is itself. |

### Sections

A section is a header line, its word and a count, then that many records, each one line but in `EXPRESSIONS`. The sections come in the order of the table, each at most once, and each may be left out. The writer leaves out an empty one. `NAMES` and `TOLERANCES` give a family after the word, one of `variable`, `function`, `constraint`, `objective`, `indicator`, `set`, `cone` and `complement`, and come at most once for each family, in that order.

| Section | Each line holds |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | No lines: the model's name follows the word. |
| `VARIABLES` | The kind, the lower bound and the upper bound of a variable. |
| `FUNCTIONS` | The constant of a function. |
| `LINEAR` | A function, a variable and its coefficient. |
| `QUADRATIC` | A function, a row, a column and the coefficient of the pair. |
| `PIECEWISE` | A pwl: the number of its points, then each point's $x$ and $y$. |
| `EXPRESSIONS` | A function and the number of postfix entries of its expression, then one line for each entry: its operator, its argument and the values the operator takes. |
| `CONSTRAINTS` | A function, the lower bound and the upper bound. |
| `OBJECTIVES` | A function, the sense, the priority, the weight, the absolute tolerance and the relative tolerance. |
| `INDICATORS` | A binary variable, the value 0 or 1, a function, the lower bound and the upper bound. |
| `SETS` | The kind, the number of members, then each member's variable and weight. |
| `CONES` | The kind, the number of functions and the functions, then the number of parameters and the parameters. |
| `COMPLEMENTS` | A function, the lower bound, the upper bound and the multiplier. |
| `NAMES` | An index in the family and its name, the indices increasing. |
| `TOLERANCES` | An index in the family, its absolute tolerance and its relative tolerance, `none` for a part left unset but not for both, the indices increasing. |

The count of `LINEAR` and `QUADRATIC` is the number of terms; the terms of one function may come in any order. The postfix entries are those `BIYOS_addexpr` takes, the positions `ref` names counted over the whole section. A pwl is named by its line in `PIECEWISE`, from 0. The writer writes only the expressions that functions hold, so nodes no function uses are left out, and a node used more than once is written once and named again.

Each section is checked as the C API checks the same records. A record the model refuses gives `BIYOS_ERR_BADFILE` at the header line of its section, with the model's message.

### Writing {#sec-native-writing}

The writer refuses a model with a callback with `BIYOS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, naming the first, before the file is made. Options set on the model are left out with one warning event from module `io`, with the field `file`. Hooks are not part of the problem and are left out with no event.

```
BIYOS 1
NAME small\20model
VARIABLES 2
cont 0 inf
bin 0 1
FUNCTIONS 2
0
0
LINEAR 2
0 0 1
0 1 2
EXPRESSIONS 1
1 2
var 0
exp 1
CONSTRAINTS 1
0 -inf 4
OBJECTIVES 1
1 min 0 1 0 0
NAMES variable 1
0 x
END
```
